issues.issue: Was the Port Authority obliged to name the decision-maker, and what follows from failing to?
issues.applicant_position: Fairness requires that the affected party know who made the decision; the Port Authority must name who terminated its licence (Wah Shing).
issues.respondent_position: No obligation to name the decision-maker; relies on Wihksne, Gramaglia and Gosselin.
issues.result_quote: Accordingly, the court finds that when this application was filed, Kimberly Transport would have been entitled to the relief sought

issues.issue: Is the application for judicial review timely, or should time be extended?
issues.applicant_position: Time ran from the implied refusal after the September 24, 2014 request, so the application is in time; alternatively, extend time.
issues.respondent_position: The 30-day period began August 22, 2014, so the application is late and an extension is needed; no reasons for the delay given.
issues.result_quote: For these reasons, I will order that this application for judicial review is timely

issues.issue: What relief should be ordered: mandamus, or an extension of time to bring judicial review of the merits?
issues.applicant_position: Sought mandamus to name the decision-maker; conceded mandamus is no longer appropriate and asked for an extension to challenge the merits.
issues.respondent_position: Mandamus would not have issued because the CUPE test was not met; no explanation for delay since November 28, 2014.
issues.result_quote: the appropriate remedy is to extend the time for Kimberly Transport to file an application to judicially review the merits
